title: Falsification-attack output (engage-crucible Step 3)
description: Output of each falsification-attack subagent. ONE attack output per hypothesis. The attacker's role is constructive (not rhetorical): propose the cheapest experiment that would discriminate the assigned hypothesis from its sibling hypotheses. Borrowed structurally from /spar-exocortex's failing-input attack and adapted for scientific reasoning.

assignedHypothesisId.description: The hypothesis this attacker is paired with.

discriminatingPrediction.description: A specific prediction the assigned hypothesis makes that no sibling makes (or makes with substantially different magnitude/direction). This is the constructive contribution — the wedge that pries the hypotheses apart.

siblingHypothesesRuledOutByDiscriminatin.description: List of sibling hypothesis ids whose probability would meaningfully drop if the discriminating prediction holds. Must include at least one — an attack that rules out zero siblings is not discriminating.

experimentalSetup.description: Re-uses one of the experimental-design artefact schemas (PICO / PECO / generic-experimental-setup) for the proposed discriminating experiment. Validator checks artefactType field but does not deep-validate the artefact body here — that is the artefact-schema's job.

expectedInformationGain.description: Qualitative ranking acceptable. Full Bayesian computation optional.

costEstimate.description: Qualitative cost tier. Cost is measured in dollars+time+ethical-risk combined, not pure dollar amount.

rationale.description: ≤200-word narrative justifying the discriminating-prediction choice and the cost ranking.
